ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014, Law No. 8 of 2015, and Law No. 162 of 2020, together with its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2003, as amended; Law No. 159 of 1981 on Joint Stock Companies, Partnerships Limited by Shares and Limited Liability Companies, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018; implementing rules of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020; Financial Regulatory Authority AML/CFT rulebooks; Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) directives and reporting thresholds; FATF Recommendations applicable through Egypt's membership of MENAFATF.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the foreign corporate shareholder's Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum/Articles of Association (required for UBO piercing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or registrar in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization - Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961; authentication chain: notary public in origin country, certification by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin country, then legalization by the Embassy/Consulate General of the Arab Republic of Egypt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution of the corporate shareholder authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and appointing the Egyptian legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization - notarization in origin country, certification by the competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalization by the Egyptian Consulate; origin-country apostille acceptable only if the origin country is an Apostille Contracting State and the receiving Egyptian authority confirms acceptance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and official identification of each UBO and each proposed director/manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent nationality authority or notary public in the document origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Consular Legalization through the Egyptian Consulate, followed by Arabic translation by a certified legal translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each UBO and corporate shareholder (KYC corroboration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Consular Legalization where required by the Egyptian Consulate; Arabic certified translation mandatory for filing with GAFI

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney executed in favor of the Egyptian incorporation agent or attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the origin country and the Egyptian Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization - notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification in the origin country, then Egyptian Consulate legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the domestic list maintained by the EMLCU under Law No. 80 of 2002 and its Executive Regulations; mandatory identification of domestic and foreign PEPs with risk-sensitive Enhanced Due Diligence covering source of wealth and source of funds; ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening at least annually or within 24 hours of any relevant list update; all screening results documented in a written AML compliance file available to GAFI, EMLCU, and the Egyptian Tax Authority on request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Unified Services e-Portal - company name availability and reservation service (gafi.gov.eg), integrated with the national Commercial Registry database administered under the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be stated in Arabic in the Memorandum of Association; a foreign-language transliteration or tradename, including an English brand, is permitted only in addition to and not instead of the Arabic name in the constitutive documents and on company signage. The name must not duplicate or be confusingly similar to any existing registered name; must not contain the full name of a natural person who is not a founding shareholder; must not be contrary to public order or misleading as to the company's objects or legal form; and must not imply regulated financial, governmental, or public functions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name rejection is communicated through the GAFI e-portal with stated grounds. The applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the GAFI Companies Registration Unit within 15 working days of rejection, attaching justification and, where applicable, a notarized authorization or disclaimer letter from the holder of a conflicting name. If the initial reconsideration is denied, the applicant may lodge an administrative appeal before the competent Administrative Court (Council of State) within 60 days of the final administrative refusal. The applicant may simultaneously reserve an alternative permissible name. A reserved name may be renewed for one additional 30-day period upon payment of the renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as the statutory registered head office. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require the LLC to maintain a physical address in Egypt evidenced by a notarized or legally stamped lease or a title deed; the office must be capable of receiving official correspondence and of being visited by GAFI, the Egyptian Tax Authority, the Commercial Registry, and customs/GOEIC officials. Virtual-office or co-working postal addresses may be used only as secondary business correspondence addresses and cannot satisfy the registered office requirement for the incorporation file, the tax card, or the GOEIC import registration certificate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-low: approximately 25-30% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months following incorporation, based on GAFI, commercial registry, and Egyptian Tax Authority risk-based inspection protocols. The likelihood increases to approximately 70% if the company proceeds with GOEIC import registration for physical importation of acetate eyeglass frames, because GOEIC verifies the registered premises and storage capacity before issuing the import registration certificate.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Egyptian Companies Law), as amended, governing Limited Liability Companies under Articles 507-556; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Articles 1-6 and Executive Regulations establishing GAFI One-Stop Shop registration procedure; Egyptian Civil Code and Commercial Registry regulations for trade name and registration formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investor Services Center and Commercial Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: GAFI Incorporation Application Form and Commercial Registry Entry Application (Notification of Establishment) with attached notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Egyptian Limited Liability Company has no statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement; the capital determined in the Articles of Association must be fully subscribed. Where cash capital is contributed prior to incorporation, it must be deposited in a temporary bank account opened with a licensed Egyptian bank and held as an escrow/deposit block until the company receives its Commercial Register certificate and the blocked funds are released to the company treasury.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The share capital of EGP [amount], divided into [number] equal shares, be and is hereby subscribed, issued and allocated to the founding shareholders as set out in the Memorandum of Association. RESOLVED FURTHER: The registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [address], Cairo, Egypt. RESOLVED FURTHER: [Name] be and is hereby appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] Company Secretary, with full authority to execute incorporation documents, open bank accounts, instruct GAFI, and make all statutory filings. RESOLVED FURTHER: The Chairman and CEO be and are hereby authorized to execute the Articles, pay all registration fees and take any lawful step necessary to complete incorporation and obtain operating approvals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop / Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Arabic trade name together with a Latin transliteration through the GAFI online name reservation module or at the Investor Services Center. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must reflect the lawful wholesale activity. Pay the published name reservation fee and collect the name reservation certificate, valid for a period specified by GAFI.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all founders and managers
Proposed Arabic trade name with Latin transliteration
Power of attorney if submission is made through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on conflict or similarity grounds, file a written objection with GAFI's Commercial Registry committee supported by a preliminary search report and submit two alternative names for immediate re-screening.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Ma'mourya Tawthiq) under the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association for the Limited Liability Company specifying the corporate name, objectives, capital, share valuations, manager appointment and registered office. Arrange for all founding shareholders to appear personally before the Egyptian Notary Public to authenticate their signatures. Obtain certified notarized copies for subsequent submission to GAFI.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
Valid passports of all founding shareholders
Name reservation certificate issued by GAFI
Declaration of lawful source of funds if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies discrepancies or insufficient signatures, correct the document accordingly, arrange re-execution by the required parties and pay the supplemental notarial fee to process the corrected version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing through GAFI One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI - One-Stop Shop / Commercial Registry Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original notarized constitutional documents, name reservation certificate, corporate lease or title registration for the registered office, and bank deposit certificate if cash capital has been paid. Complete GAFI Incorporation Application Form, pay the statutory registration and official gazette publication fees, and await issuance of the Commercial Register certificate, incorporation certificate and, where applicable, GAFI operating record for the licensed wholesale activity.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
GAFI name reservation certificate
Bank deposit certificate for paid-up cash capital (if any)
Lease contract or proof of registered office location
Passport copies and signatures of all founders
Completed GAFI Form 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query or request for additional clarification, respond in writing within ten working days with a memorandum and supplementary documents. If the matter is not cured, file an internal appeal to the GAFI Investment Disputes and Grievances Committee for re-examination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the Egyptian Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - linked GAFI One-Stop Shop window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Commercial Register certificate, submit the tax registration application to the Egyptian Tax Authority office designated by GAFI. Register for income tax, payroll tax, and value added tax if the anticipated annual turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed the VAT registration threshold. Obtain the Tax Card (Bitaqa Dhareebiya) evidencing the company's tax file number.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register certificate
Notarized Articles of Association
Lease contract for registered office
Manager's passport or national ID
Tax registration application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Card issuance is delayed, escalate to the Central Administration of Taxpayer Services through the GAFI liaison officer and obtain a written acknowledgement with a definitive issuance date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Capital Release
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian Bank under the supervision of the Central Bank of Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approach an Egypt-licensed commercial bank after incorporation with the board resolution and Commercial Register certificate. Complete customer due diligence forms, identify all authorized signatories, and open the corporate current account. Transfer or deposit any paid-up capital from the temporary escrow/blocked account into the company account and obtain a bank account certificate for filing with GAFI or ETA if required.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register certificate and Tax Card
Board resolution appointing authorized signatories and authorizing bank account opening
Passport copies of all signatories and beneficial owners
Notarized Articles of Association
Lease contract or utility bill evidencing physical address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced KYC documentation, provide affidavits as to source of wealth and supporting financial statements of shareholders. If the bank still refuses, apply concurrently to another licensed bank and inform the GAFI desk of the bank's delay for administrative intervention.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Premises Occupancy, Civil Defense and No-Industrial-License Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil Defense Authority (Fire Safety) and Local Municipal Licensing Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the office or warehouse lease and layout plan to the Civil Defense Authority for fire safety inspection. Ensure fire extinguishers, emergency exits and basic safety signage are in place and obtain the fire safety certificate. Obtain municipal occupancy clearance for commercial/administrative use. As the activity is limited to wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames with no manufacturing operations, confirm in writing that no Industrial Development Authority license and no environmental impact assessment are required.
required_dossiers: Lease contract and proof of ownership by the landlord
Premises layout plan and utility bills
Fire safety self-check report
Commercial Register certificate and Articles of Association
Completed Civil Defense inspection application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Civil Defense inspection fails, remedy the stated fire safety deficiencies and reschedule the inspection. If the municipality questions the commercial-use classification, submit the GAFI operating record and lease amendment expressly restricting use to wholesale warehousing and administration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) of the Ministry of Trade and Industry - not applicable to a pure wholesale distributor of eyeglass frames; no manufacturing license required
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license required; the Commercial Register entry under ISIC 4646 as 'Wholesale of Ophthalmic Eyewear Frames' is the sole statutory authorization for commercial operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category C (no industrial or manufacturing activity; wholesale distribution and administrative office use only)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, volatile organic compound or industrial emissions thresholds applicable to the activity. If packaging waste is generated, comply with waste management requirements under Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended, and its executive regulations by segregating recyclable cardboard and plastic and engaging a licensed waste carrier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Civil Defense Authority and an occupancy clearance from the local municipal licensing office is required for the registered office and warehouse. The workplace must undergo a structural load inspection only if heavy shelving is installed, and occupational health declarations under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 must be posted and delivered to the competent labor office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance - official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned LLC must register with the Egyptian Tax Authority at the competent tax office having jurisdiction over its Egyptian head office or place of effective management. Required filings include the incorporation contract, commercial registry extract (including foreign ownership details), board resolution appointing a tax representative if non-resident, power of attorney for the representative, lease or ownership evidence of the Egyptian premises, and valid IDs of managers and shareholders. The ETA issues a unified tax card and separate VAT registration number. Application must be made before commencing taxable activity, and a tax file number is obtained after document review, on-site inspection where necessary, and issuance of the compliance card.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or free-standing entity classification election exists under Egyptian domestic tax law. Egyptian LLCs are automatically treated as taxable persons at entity level under Law No. 91 of 2005. No domestic hybrid mismatch election is available; foreign transparent entities may be recharacterized by reference to the applicable double tax treaty and the ordinary principles of the Egyptian Income Tax Law. The LLC may elect to register for VAT within the statutory period upon exceeding the registration threshold, but substance and legal form govern classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 in annual taxable supplies for goods or services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates phased real-time ETA e-invoicing under the electronic invoice and electronic receipt regime. Invoices must be generated in the ETA-compliant XML/JSON format, submitted through the ETA integration APIs or approved service-provider portal, validated and cleared in close-to-real-time before issuance to the buyer, and carry a unique ETA approval code and embedded QR barcode. Intra-Community-style clearance, digital stamping, and rejection handling are required under Ministerial Decree No. 491 of 2022 and subsequent amendments. All tax invoices and credit/debit notes must be digitally signed and transmitted; non-compliant invoices are treated as non-deductible and may block customs and tax clearances.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported tangible goods, including acetate eyeglass frames, are eligible for zero-rating when title has passed to a foreign buyer, the goods physically leave Egypt to a destination outside Egypt through customs procedures, payment is received in convertible foreign currency through banking channels, and the exporter retains complete documentation proving the export transaction. Services physically rendered outside Egypt or directly related to exported goods may also be zero-rated under the VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 where the recipient is outside Egypt and the benefit is consumed abroad. The exporter must be a registered VAT person and must file the export lists and supporting schedules electronically.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and Customs Authority may conduct joint audits of export zero-rating, reviewing bank receipts, customs manifests, freight documents, purchase records, and internal costing. Circumvention, fictitious exports, overstatement of export values, forged remittance certificates, or failure to repatriate proceeds within the prescribed 180-day deadline result in reversal of zero-rating, immediate assessment of VAT at 14% plus late-payment and delay penalties, monetary fines up to the amount of tax evaded, suspension of the taxpayer's e-invoicing capability, and potential criminal prosecution with imprisonment under Law No. 67 of 2016. Retroactive clawback may extend to prior tax periods where documentary fraud is proven.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), exercising exclusive foreign-exchange regulation through the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020 (CBBL), as amended, and CBE Board of Directors' circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since the March 2024 unification, the Egyptian Pound is formally market-determined under a flexible exchange-rate regime supported by the IMF Extended Fund Facility. Current-account transactions (goods trade, freight, insurance, commissions, and profit remittance against verified audited earnings) are freely convertible for licensed corporate clients subject to full banking documentation. Capital-account transactions remain regulated: foreign-direct-investment equity injections, intercompany loan servicing, liquidation proceeds, and portfolio repatriation require a CBE-licensed bank channel, GAFI registration documentation, and proof of original entry of funds; portfolio inflows additionally use the CBE Repatriation Mechanism. For the optical-frames wholesale LLC, dividend repatriation from genuine audited export earnings is lawful, but procedural hurdles include un-matched import/export customs declarations, unsettled withholding tax (10% domestic rate, often reduced to 5% under Egypt's double-taxation agreements), and the bank's demand for a complete source-of-wealth file for the foreign shareholder. There is no legal incompatibility with profit remittance; operational friction is documentary, not convertibility-based.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods exporters must repatriate the full value of export proceeds into an Egyptian-licensed bank account within 90 calendar days from the shipment date (bill of lading or airway bill date, as applicable). No mandatory fixed-ratio surrender or compulsory conversion to EGP is currently imposed under the market-determined regime; proceeds may be retained in a foreign-currency account with an Egyptian bank or converted to EGP at the interbank market rate. Exporters must maintain the evidential chain comprising the customs export declaration, beneficiary commercial invoice, bill of lading, and incoming SWIFT MT103. Failure to meet the 90-day window exposes the entity to CBE monetary penalties, bank negative-list classification, and suspension of trade-finance and FX facilities.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility. Under the CBBL and CBE implementing rules, resident commercial entities must receive and discharge foreign-currency obligations through CBE-licensed banks; routing export proceeds to an offshore EMI (Payoneer, Wise Business, Airwallex, Mercury, Currencycloud) as a principal collection account violates the 90-day repatriation requirement and creates a China-risk compliance gap for the local bank. An offshore EMI may be tolerated only as a minor convenience layer for incidental low-value receipts, provided funds are promptly swept to the Egyptian corporate account and fully disclosed. The mandatory primary clearing rail for acetate optical-frame wholesale trade remains a resident foreign-currency account at an Egyptian Tier-1 bank with full SWIFT participation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory. For a foreign-owned EG_LLC, the legal representative and each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) must complete in-person CDD identity verification at the Egyptian branch; remote video-KYC is not accepted for non-resident UBOs by the Tier-1 banks. A non-resident director may appoint a local resident manager via a Power of Attorney notarized in the director's jurisdiction and legalized by the Egyptian Consulate, but the granting director's passport and the POA must still be physically verified and a compliance interview may be required. Local branches will additionally demand the original Commercial Registry extract, active tax card, GAFI investment certificate, statistical card (for export activity), board resolution appointing signatories, and audited opening balance after activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contribution originating from a personal offshore account or a jurisdiction with weak beneficial-ownership transparency, or any indication of crypto-derived funds in the source.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 6-12 months of bank statements of the remitting account; SWIFT sender confirmations; notarized statement of source of wealth; audited financial statements of the shareholder or certified personal net-worth statement; tax clearance or tax certificates on the capital; corporate chart of the direct shareholder; apostilled or consular-legalized incorporation documents; explicit written declaration of non-involvement of crypto assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade counterparty exposure to high-risk or sanctions-affected jurisdictions (e.g., Syria, Sudan, Libya) or unvetted non-face-to-face acetate frame suppliers in Asia with opaque ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed bank counterparty due-diligence questionnaire for each supplier and key buyer; commercial registration and UBO details of counterparties; end-user/end-beneficiary declarations; export certificates of origin; sanctions-screening report from a recognized compliance database (LexisNexis, Refinitiv World-Check, Dow Jones); GOEIC import/export registration; written exclusion policy covering OFAC/UN/EU-restricted jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the declared wholesale distribution purpose and projected cash-flow profile, including rapid onward payments to third-country processors or trade-chain layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed distribution agreements; full purchase-order set; commercial invoices; transport documents (bill of lading/air waybill); customs entries; warehouse lease or logistics contracts; corporate organizational chart describing the group trade flow; written business model narrative; historical bank reference letters from anchor buyers or the parent company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or adverse-media flags on a UBO, director, or authorized signatory, and any unexplained mismatch in beneficial-ownership declarations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal PEP declaration; public-office role letters; independent source-of-wealth report; legalized passport copies; audited trail of the ownership chain from the entity to each natural person; legal opinion from an Egyptian counsel confirming ownership percentages; bank reference from a regulated foreign financial institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: non-resident shareholder issues an outgoing SWIFT MT103 wire to the EG_LLC designated account at an Egyptian Tier-1 bank, currency USD or EUR, with field 70 explicitly stating the purpose: 'EQUITY INJECTION FOR SHARE CAPITAL - LLCOWNER - [Company Commercial Registry number]'. Egyptian banks do not use IBAN; the beneficiary field must carry the exact local account number plus the bank's SWIFT/BIC. The receiving bank will classify the inflow under the CBE Balance-of-Payments code 'Direct Investment - Equity', issue a foreign-currency inflow certificate or capital-fund certificate, and record the investment in the company's file. The company must file the capital increase with GAFI and, where applicable, update its commercial registry paid-in capital; any EGP conversion is executed at the prevailing interbank rate. The inflow certificate and GAFI stamp become the essential documents for future dividend and liquidation repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 direct telegraphic transfer for routine consignments and low-risk established suppliers. For major acetate and stock-frame supply contracts, an irrevocable commercial documentary letter of credit (SWIFT MT700, at-sight, usually with a confirming bank requested) is the recommended rail, with documentary collection (MT400/MT202) permissible for recurring low-risk suppliers. Each outflow requires a valid importer registration with GOEIC, an active tax card, the underlying pro-forma or commercial invoice, and the customs bill of entry after clearing; the Egyptian bank converts EGP at market rate and debits the USD account. The bank may repurchase the EGP against the company's export repatriation record to satisfy netting and CBE reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP outright forward contract, generally available up to 12 months against evidenced current-account trade exposure, booked under an ISDA/CSA or bank master agreement.
USD/EGP cross-currency swap (CCS) for matched import/export contract flows, available from Tier-1 banks and subject to CBE reporting and, for tenors beyond 12 months, prior CBE approval.

Offshore USD/EGP non-deliverable forward (NDF): lawful only for non-resident counterparties or with explicit CBE authorization; Egyptian-resident corporates of the optical-frames LLC type may not lawfully transact onshore business through offshore NDFs, and onshore NDF booking is not currently authorized by the CBE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 19 for legal persons) with audited financial statements, tax computations, and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 calendar months after the fiscal year end (April 30 for a December 31 year-end); a justified 2-month extension may be granted by the ETA; electronic filing is mandatory via the ETA online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a fine of EGP 500 to EGP 2,000 plus EGP 100 per month of delay and default interest on tax due; the ETA may issue an estimated assessment after a 15-day notice; sustained non-filing leads to enforced collection procedures and criminal liability for willful tax evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements with the Auditor's report and the General Assembly approval resolution (GAFI Investment-Law compliance filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year end, following the annual General Assembly meeting required by Law No. 159 of 1981
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Warnings and administrative fines up to EGP 1,000 per the Investment Law schedule; repeated non-submission suspends GAFI incentives and privileges and may result in deregistration from GAFI records with referral for administrative strike-off of the commercial registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry renewal of the company's registration record and certificate validity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and March 31; the commercial registration certificate expires on December 31 of each prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewed registration becomes inactive, blocking notarized contracts, customs clearances, banking KYC, and tax clearance certificates; continued non-renewal prevents the company from performing registered commercial activity and authorizes the Commercial Registry to delete the record, triggering administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Card (taxpayer identification certificate) renewal and tax file update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority - competent tax office (Tax Services Department)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the first quarter (January to March); card validity aligns with the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a valid tax card blocks VAT input credit recovery, customs clearances, bank account formalities, and government procurement; the ETA may impose fines for transactions executed without a valid tax card and may suspend the tax file, leading to enforced collection and a negative compliance record that delays future tax clearance certificates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value-Added Tax reconciliation declaration (annual VAT summary return) supporting the monthly VAT filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the fiscal year end; monthly VAT returns remain separately due by the end of each succeeding month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false annual VAT reconciliation triggers fines under the VAT Law (up to EGP 5,000), monthly delay interest of 2% on unpaid VAT, and the risk of ETA estimated assessment; persistent non-compliance results in VAT registration cancellation and consequential administrative strike-off referrals

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Egyptian LLC must appoint an auditor when share capital exceeds EGP 50,000, when partners exceed 10, or when partners holding at least 10% of the capital request an audit (Law No. 159 of 1981, Art. 102); an entity registered with GAFI under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 must in all cases have annual financial statements audited by a licensed auditor registered with the Egyptian Financial Supervisory Authority and file the audited statements with GAFI irrespective of size
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory financial statements are prepared under Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are substantially aligned with IFRS; IFRS is additionally acceptable for consolidation and reporting packages required by foreign parents

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Egyptian law, LLC quota transfer becomes binding upon the company only after entry in the Register of Partners, which must be updated at each transfer and formally confirmed at the annual General Assembly (Law No. 159 of 1981, Art. 47; minutes recorded in the Minute Book). Under the AML regime (Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended, and FIU regulations), the company must maintain an Ultimate Beneficial Owner register identifying natural persons holding, directly or indirectly, at least 25% of capital or voting rights or exercising control by other means, update the register within 30 days of any transfer, and provide an annual UBO confirmation to the registered office and, upon request, to GAFI, the FIU, banks, or the Commercial Registry; notarized transfer deeds are required for third-party enforceability.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 250-700 per year (Egyptian registered-office/agent services for a GAFI-registered LLC)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,200-2,800 per audit cycle for a small to mid-sized wholesale trading LLC (fee set in EGP by the audit firm)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax holidays and preferential rates in free zones (e.g. 0% for 5-10 years in Suez Canal Economic Zone for qualifying manufacturing or qualifying activities)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Tax Authority Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 100 series) via e-Tax Portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end (standard deadline 31 March for calendar year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit after allowable deductions, depreciation and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egypt-sourced income; non-residents file via withholding agent or direct submission with TRC

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business expenses, interest, R&D, bad debts and statutory deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Limited to attributable Egyptian income; foreign expenses require substantiation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign taxes withheld on dividends, royalties and interest
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits under DTAA or domestic rules

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty 1% of tax due per month of delay (maximum 10%), plus 2% per month interest on unpaid tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from Egyptian Tax Authority, submit DTAA claim form with supporting documents to reduce or eliminate WHT at source
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory (0-10% under most DTAs); Interest: 15% statutory (reduced to 0-10% under DTAs)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egyptian Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) require adequate local management, employees, premises and risks to substantiate tax residency and prevent recharacterisation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understatement of taxable income or inflation of deductible expenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty: fine equal to 100% of evaded tax plus imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors personally liable for restitution, fines and possible imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Lack of adequate local employees, premises or decision-making functions in Egypt
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment to deemed profit, penalties up to 100% of tax benefit, possible deregistration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several liability; possible travel bans and civil claims

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or file Local File / Master File when turnover exceeds threshold
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty EGP 50,000 to EGP 500,000 plus interest on underpaid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for penalties and potential criminal referral

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to apply DTAA relief or withholding at reduced treaty rate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax equal to difference plus 2% monthly interest and possible criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for additional tax, interest and potential imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creation of artificial entities or transactions without commercial purpose
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, penalties up to 200% of tax benefit, possible criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors face civil restitution, fines and imprisonment
